title: Scope a Useful Mobile Flow
why: Mobile tasks are shaped by small screens, interruptions, and platform conventions.
activity: Choose one task for a mobile app. Define platform, audience, lifecycle assumptions, and three acceptance examples.
evidence: A one-page app brief and flow sketch.
reflection: Which part of this task benefits from a mobile experience?

title: Build an Accessible Screen
why: An interface must remain usable when text, vision, or input needs change.
activity: Implement the main screen with native controls. Check larger text, contrast, touch targets, and screen-reader order.
evidence: A working screen and accessibility findings with fixes.
reflection: Which accessibility issue changed your layout?

title: Connect Navigation and State
why: A flow can look correct while losing user state during navigation or interruptions.
activity: Build a three-screen task. Define state ownership and verify back, cancellation, backgrounding, and returning to the task.
evidence: A state map and recorded navigation/lifecycle checks.
reflection: Where does each piece of state live, and when should it reset?

title: Keep Progress Offline
why: Users should not lose meaningful work when an app closes or connectivity changes.
activity: Persist meaningful user input locally. Kill and relaunch the app, test missing data and storage errors, and keep a local fixture if you use networking.
reflection: Which persisted value survived relaunch, and how did you verify it?

title: Extract Testable Logic
why: Separating business rules from views makes behavior easier to verify and change.
activity: Move one business rule out of views. Inject its dependencies and verify it without launching the UI.
evidence: A domain service, architecture note, and focused unit tests.
reflection: Which rule can you now test without launching the app?

title: Exercise the Complete Flow
why: Mobile defects often appear at lifecycle or device boundaries rather than the happy path.
activity: Test the primary journey and one interrupted or invalid path. Reproduce a defect and verify the fix on a simulator and, when available, a physical device.
evidence: Test cases, regression evidence, and a stated device-testing limit.
reflection: Which interrupted flow revealed a defect?

title: Profile and Handle Permissions
why: Profiling replaces guesses about performance with measurements.
activity: Profile a slow interaction. Improve a measured bottleneck; if a device API is needed, explain the permission request and test denial. If none is needed, document why.
evidence: Before/after profiling evidence and permission/fallback decisions.
reflection: What improved measurably, and what was the cost of that change?

title: Prepare an Installable Build
why: An installable build reveals release, signing, and privacy issues hidden by previews.
activity: Create an installable development build. Review signing, app icon, privacy behavior, offline use, and release configuration without claiming store approval.
evidence: An installable build and a release/privacy checklist.
reflection: Which release requirement still needs a device or distribution test?

title: Run a Usability Session
why: Watching someone complete a task reveals confusing interactions.
activity: Ask a consenting person to perform the core task. Record anonymized observations, fix one interaction, and recheck accessibility.
evidence: Task observations, UI changes, and accessibility recheck results.
reflection: Which observed difficulty did your UI change address?

title: Create a Mobile Case Study
why: A mobile portfolio should show how the app behaves beyond a polished screenshot.
activity: Explain the task, platform decisions, state, offline behavior, accessibility, performance, and release evidence. State which devices you tested.
evidence: A case study with build instructions, recordings, tests, and limitations.
reflection: What device, accessibility, or offline limitation must a reviewer know?
